security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown false positives from inline code spans, tables, and fenced examples. The confirmed risks are expected for this skill: it instructs users to install and run the RunComfy CLI, submit prompts and media references to RunComfy, and store an API token locally.

remediation.issue: External CLI installation and execution are required.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to install @runcomfy/cli only from the official package source and review the command before running it.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media URLs are sent to RunComfy infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential scripts, private voice recordings, or non-public media URLs unless their RunComfy account permits that use.

remediation.issue: RunComfy login stores an API token in a local config file.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the token file owner-only, prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in ephemeral CI environments, and rotate the token if the machine is shared or compromised.

content.value_statement: Video generation settings can be hard to choose across model families. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to run Wan 2.7 with clear prompts, lip-sync inputs, and safe output handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Wan 2.7 is a good choice for text-to-video generation.
Provides RunComfy CLI commands for default, lip-sync, and literal-control video generation.
Documents supported prompt, audio_url, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, negative prompt, expansion, and seed fields.
Gives prompt writing guidance for camera motion, primary action, negative prompts, and seed iteration.
Lists practical limitations, exit codes, output download behavior, and token storage details.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and network access.
Wan 2.7 output is limited to 15 seconds and 1080p in this skill documentation.
Audio lip-sync requires an external WAV or MP3 URL that meets the documented size and duration limits.
The skill is guidance for a hosted model and does not include local video generation code.

use_cases.title: Create short product videos
use_cases.description: Generate polished product showcase clips with camera movement, lighting direction, and negative prompts.

use_cases.title: Produce lip-synced spokesperson clips
use_cases.description: Use an audio_url voice track with a visual prompt to create short presenter-style video assets.

use_cases.title: Prototype vertical social clips
use_cases.description: Draft 9:16 video ideas with clear motion, aspect ratio, duration, and seed controls.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner default clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you want a simple Wan 2.7 video from one idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 5 second 1080p Wan 2.7 video with this prompt: [describe the scene]. Use 16:9 and include a concise negative prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-sync from audio
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you have a hosted voice track.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Wan 2.7 lip-sync video using this audio_url: [URL]. The scene should show [subject], with [camera motion], [lighting], and a duration of [seconds].

prompt_templates.title: Platform-specific variant
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when creating content for a vertical or square channel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Wan 2.7 video for [platform]. Use aspect ratio [9:16 or 1:1], duration [seconds], and a prompt focused on one clear action.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced controlled iteration
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when comparing variants with stable composition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Wan 2.7 with prompt expansion disabled, seed [number], resolution [720p or 1080p], duration [seconds], and this exact prompt: [prompt]. Avoid [specific artifacts].

output_examples.input: A product showcase prompt for a premium object on a marble surface.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a RunComfy command using Wan 2.7, a concise prompt, 1080p resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio, and an output directory.

output_examples.input: A request for a lip-synced spokesperson clip with a hosted MP3 voiceover.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a Wan 2.7 request with audio_url, matching duration, vertical aspect ratio, and a prompt focused on face, lighting, and camera stability.

output_examples.input: A request to make several controlled variants of one video concept.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends reusing a seed for comparable variants and changing the seed only when genuine visual variety is needed.

best_practices: Describe one primary action per clip and put camera motion near the start of the prompt.
Use concrete negative prompts such as no subtitles, no watermark, and no flicker.
Match audio length, duration, aspect ratio, and resolution before running the CLI command.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private voice tracks or confidential media URLs without approval.
Do not combine many unrelated actions in a single short clip prompt.
Do not disable prompt expansion unless you need literal control over the prompt.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an AI assistant to generate Wan 2.7 text-to-video requests through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI and hosted RunComfy model API.

faq.question: Can it create lip-synced videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents audio_url input for WAV or MP3 files that meet RunComfy duration and size limits.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What are the main safety considerations?
faq.answer: Users should review CLI commands, protect the RunComfy token, and avoid sending confidential prompts or media URLs.

faq.question: When should I choose another model?
faq.answer: Use another model when you need longer clips, native 4K output, in-pass voice generation, or faster iteration than Wan 2.7 provides.
